# Figma mirror audit — live file `ip2wZ3UUQ5sbFc3r902kYK` against the token layer

**Auditor:** token-keeper (owns `design-system/tokens/tokens.json` per the routing table)
**Date:** 2026-09-02 · **Token release:** 0.2.0
**Evidence:** `scratch/figma-audit/figma-variables.json` (561 variables, captured 2026-09-02)
**Corroborating evidence:** `scratch/figma-live.json` (762 variables, captured 2026-09-01 15:03, pre-collapse)
**Status:** advisory. **Nothing was modified** — not `tokens.json`, not the capture, not the generated file.

---

## Verdict

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| 1. Does the live file match `coforge.figma.tokens.json`? | **Yes — exactly.** 0 missing, 0 extra, 0 divergent across 797 value comparisons. |
| 2. Did the mode collapse lose anything? | **No values lost.** All 236 Dark aliases correct. **161 Dark `$description`s were lost** — structurally, not accidentally. |
| 3. Are the alpha primitives intact? | **Yes.** 35/35 present with exact alpha; 53/53 semantic bindings resolve through them. |
| 4. Are the dimensions px and correct? | **Yes.** 27/27 converted at 16px/rem. `size.07` = 62, `tracking.07` = −2. |
| 5. Anything in Figma not in the token layer? | **No off-system variables.** Non-variable content was not capturable — see "not verified". |
| 6. Text and effect styles | **NOT VERIFIED — no capture exists.** `scale/code` is verified *correct against the source*. |
| 7. Scopes and descriptions | **561/561 carry `ALL_SCOPES`.** Zero scoping in the entire library. |

**The mirror's content is right. Its instrumentation is broken and its shape is no longer importable.**

---

## Method — what "re-derived" means here

I did not read `coforge.figma.tokens.json` and compare it to the capture. That would prove only that
two files agree, and one of them is generated by the party being audited.

I walked `design-system/tokens/tokens.json` directly and re-implemented the bridge from
`design-system/contracts/figma-representability.json` — the type table, the drop rule, the
16px/rem conversion, the alias-path resolution — in a script that does not import
`validation/build-figma-tokens.py`. That derivation produced **797 representable tokens and 32
dropped** (8 `typography`, 4 `shadow`, 9 `duration`, 9 `cubicBezier`, 2 `coforge.levelSet`), which is
the claimed split.

I then compared my derivation to the generated file: **797/797 paths present on both sides, 0 type
mismatches, 0 value mismatches.** The generator faithfully implements the contract, so from here the
generated file can be used as shorthand for the source without begging the question.

Finally I compared my derivation to the live capture at the `(collection, name, mode)` level, mapping
`semantic.X` → mode Light and `semantic-dark.X` → mode Dark of the single collapsed collection.

| Extra in Figma | — | **0** |

| Numbers | 32 (13 spacing, 7 size, 7 tracking, 5 weight) | **32 equal**; 5 carry float32 residue ≤ 2.15 × 10⁻⁸ px |

Also verified inside the live file: **0 duplicate `(collection, name)` pairs**, **0 dangling aliases**

## 2 · The mode collapse — the highest-risk question

The Dark values were copied from a collection that has been deleted, so the usual recourse — read the
old collection — is gone. Three independent lines of evidence say nothing of value was lost.

**(a) Against the source.** All 236 Dark-mode aliases match `tokens.json`'s `semantic-dark` group
name-by-name, with zero exceptions. All 236 Light-mode aliases match `semantic`.

**(b) The Dark mode is not a duplicate of Light.** `tokens.json` says Light and Dark should alias the
*same* palette entry for exactly **13** of the 236 names. In Figma, Light and Dark are identical for
exactly **13** names, and they are the same 13. A copy that had silently duplicated Light into Dark
would show 236; a copy that dropped Dark would show a different set. Neither happened.

**(c) Against the pre-collapse capture.** `scratch/figma-live.json` — taken 2026-09-01 15:03, when
`semantic-dark` was still its own collection — holds all 236 dark names. Comparing the two captures,
24 hours and one collapse apart, produced by different capture scripts:

- names missing from the new capture: **0**; names added: **0**
- Dark aliases that changed: **29**. Light aliases that changed: **24**. Total **53**.
- **every one of the 53** is of the form `palette.X` → `palette.X-aNN` — the C-021 repair, and nothing else
- palette gained exactly **35** variables, all alpha-suffixed, and lost none
- the 254 surviving palette literals: **0 changed**
- `typography`, `spacing`, `density`: 0 added, 0 removed, 0 changed

Two captures, one source and the git history all agree on what moved and why.

### What the collapse *did* lose

**161 of 236 semantic tokens carry a Dark-specific `$description` in `tokens.json` that Figma can no
longer hold.** A Figma variable has one description; it is not per-mode. In all 161 cases the live
file carries the **Light** description.

Of those 161: **137 are machine filler** on the source side (`"01. Token for 01 in the design
system."`) and losing them costs nothing. **24 are substantive prose about dark behaviour** —
`background-inverse-hover`, `background-selected-hover`, `icon.interactive`, `ai.inner-shadow`,
`ai.aura-start`, `ai.aura-end`, `ai.border-start`, `ai.border-end`, `ai.border-strong`,
`ai.drop-shadow`, `ai.aura-hover-background`, and 13 more.

This is recoverable today, because `tokens.json` is upstream. It stops being recoverable at the ADR-001
inversion point, when Figma becomes the owner and the repo mirrors: 24 descriptions with no Figma home
cannot be mirrored from a file that does not hold them. See finding **E-1**.

## 7 · Scopes and descriptions

**All 561 variables carry `scopes: ["ALL_SCOPES"]`. Not most — all.**

A designer opening a fill picker sees 289 palette primitives beside 236 semantic tokens with nothing
distinguishing the layer they are supposed to use from the layer they are not. Every numeric field —
corner radius, stroke weight, line height, opacity — offers all 13 spacing steps, all 7 font sizes, all
7 tracking values and all 5 weights, none of which belong there. The layering that the token
architecture spends 236 aliases establishing is invisible at the only place a designer meets it.

Nothing in this repository declares, generates or checks scopes. See **W-2**.

Descriptions: 27 of 561 diverge from what the generator emits today — see **W-1**. The remaining 534
match exactly.

## Findings

### BLOCKER

**B-1 · `check-figma-live.py`, the only instrument that can detect Figma drift, is now blind in one direction and screaming in the other.**

Run against this capture it reports **474 blockers and 323 uncompared** on a mirror that is, by the
re-derivation above, exact. Two independent causes:

1. It reads `c.modes[0]` only. **Dark mode is structurally invisible to it.** The half of the mirror
   that is unrecoverable if it drifts is the half the checker cannot see, and it will report PASS while
   never having looked.
2. The capture schema changed from `{alias, value}` to `{modes: {mode: {...}}}`. The checker finds no
   `alias` key, concludes every aliased variable holds a literal, and emits 474 false blockers. It does
   not notice that it is reading a shape it does not understand.

It also reports `MISSING from Figma` for all 236 `semantic-dark.*` paths, which is B-2 surfacing here.

This is ranked above everything else because every other finding is a thing that is currently *fine*.
This is the thing that guarantees the next divergence is not caught. And it fails in the crying-wolf
direction: 474 false blockers on a perfect mirror is how a check gets ignored, which is worse than a
check that is merely absent, because absence is at least visible.

*Suggested fix:* teach it modes (compare every mode, not `modes[0]`); teach it the capture schema; and
add a shape assertion so an unrecognised capture format **fails as unreadable** rather than being
interpreted as 474 findings. The repo's own principle applies exactly — a value this check cannot read
is not a value it has verified, and a *format* it cannot read is not a file it has checked.

**B-2 · `coforge.figma.tokens.json` still describes a two-collection world and is no longer safe to import.**

The contract's `one_import_source` rule makes this file the only thing Figma imports. It still emits
`semantic` and `semantic-dark` as parallel top-level groups. Importing it into the live file today
would recreate `semantic-dark` as a separate collection — 236 duplicate variables — while the Dark mode
of the collapsed `semantic` collection went unmaintained and silently stale. The single most likely
future action on this file is the one that breaks it.

The root cause is that **nothing in the repository declares Figma modes at all.**
`figma-representability.json` has a `dimension_unit` section because rem/px cost a correction; it has
no `modes` section, because modes had not been used until today. The collapse was performed in Figma
by Plugin API and left no trace on the repo side.

*Suggested fix:* add a `modes` block to `figma-representability.json` declaring that `semantic-dark.*`
is mode `Dark` of collection `semantic` and `semantic.*` is mode `Light`; make the generator emit a
mode-aware shape; until then, mark the generated file **not re-importable** in its own `$description`
so the warning travels with the file. Gate A — this changes what the bridge means, not just what it
contains.

### ERROR

**E-1 · 161 Dark descriptions have no Figma representation, and 24 of them are real.**

Covered in §2. A Figma variable holds one description, not one per mode; the Light text won in all 161
cases. Harmless while the repo is upstream. At the ADR-001 inversion it becomes a permanent loss of 24
pieces of dark-theme guidance, because a mirror cannot mirror what the master does not hold.

*Suggested fix:* declare in `figma-representability.json` that `$description` is per-variable and that
the Light description is canonical; then, before inversion, either fold the dark-specific sentence into
the single description (`"… Dark: uses a heavier alpha so the shadow reads against the dark ground."`)
or record the 24 as an accepted loss with a named owner. Separately, the **137 filler descriptions** on
the `semantic-dark` side are a token-layer quality finding in their own right: the dark half of the
colour layer is documented markedly worse than the light half, and the collapse has made that
invisible rather than fixing it.

### WARNING

**W-2 · Zero scoping across 561 variables.** Detailed in §7. The largest usability gap in the
foundations library, and the report notes correctly that nothing here checks it.
*Suggested fix:* add a `scopes` declaration to `figma-representability.json` keyed by token root —
`spacing.*` → `GAP, WIDTH_HEIGHT`; `typography.size.*` → `FONT_SIZE`; `tracking.*` → `LETTER_SPACING`;
`weight.*` → `FONT_WEIGHT`; `family.*` → `FONT_FAMILY`; `semantic.*` colour scoped by name segment
(`border.*` → `STROKE_COLOR`, `text.*`/`icon.*` → `TEXT_FILL`, the rest → `FRAME_FILL, SHAPE_FILL`);
`palette.*` narrowed or hidden from publishing so the semantic layer is what a designer reaches. Then
teach the generator to emit it and this audit to check it. Gate A — a new declaration, not a sync.

**W-1 · The live variables were not written by the current generated file.** Values agree; provenance
does not. 27 dimension descriptions carry an **older wording** of the rem/px note — live reads
`"[px. Source token is 0.125rem; Figma has no rem unit, so the bridge converts dimensions at 16px/rem…]"`
where the generator emits `"[0.125rem in the source. Figma has no rem; the bridge converts at 16px/rem…]"`.
And 5 tracking values carry float32 residue (`0.1599999964237213`) computed from a `tokens.json` that
held `0.009999999776482582`, where the file today holds a clean `0.01`. Both prove the live dimensions
are the residue of the 2026-08-31 hand-fix plus plugin edits, not of an import of
`coforge.figma.tokens.json`. **The import path this repository documents as the mechanism has never
actually produced the live file.** Nothing is wrong with the values; what is wrong is that the
provenance story is unevidenced, and an unexercised path is not a working path.
*Suggested fix:* after B-2 is repaired, perform one clean import from the generated file and re-capture,
so provenance and content agree. Until then, say so in the contract's `enforced_by` note.

**W-3 · Two of four shadow tokens declare a Figma home that does not exist.** All four `shadow` tokens
carry `figma_home: figma-effect-style`, but only 2 effect styles exist. `elevation.surface.flat` and
`elevation.surface.raised` are materialised; `elevation.shadow.none` and `elevation.shadow.raised`,
which the surface pair pure-aliases, are not. Not materialising both is *correct* — it would duplicate
— but the contract says `figma_home` names "a real Figma primitive the token should be materialised
into," so two tokens make a declaration that is false as written.
*Suggested fix:* add a `materialised_via` field pointing the base tokens at the surface aliases, or
soften the contract's wording. (Unverified in the live file — style count is taken from the brief.)

**W-4 · `elevation.shadow.raised`'s description is stale in the favourable direction.** It states its
colour "aliases the existing `semantic.shadow` (light theme) — a parallel dark-theme geometry primitive
is not authored here." Post-collapse, `semantic.shadow` is one mode-aware variable, so an effect style
bound to it follows the theme automatically. The source under-claims what Figma now does, and a reader
would reasonably conclude dark shadows are unhandled when they are.
*Suggested fix:* update the description. Gate A.

**W-5 · The tracking curve's stated 1:1 pairing has an undocumented exception.** The
`typography.tracking` group description asserts the curve is "Paired 1:1 by index with
typography.size." `scale.code` breaks it: `size.01` with `tracking.03`, where `caption` uses `size.01`
with `tracking.01`. This is defensible — a mono face at 12px does not want the +0.16px a proportional
face wants — and Figma is correct to bind it that way. But the rule as written is inaccurate, and the
exception is nowhere. This brief anticipated the binding would look like a bug; it looks like a bug
because the source stopped describing itself accurately.
*Suggested fix:* add the exception to the tracking group description in `tokens.json`. Gate A.

**W-6 · The Figma file is not in `validation/published-surfaces.json`.** That registry exists so a
published surface making claims about this system carries a `documents` anchor and goes stale *by
definition* rather than by someone noticing. A shared variables library asserting the entire token
layer is the most consequential published surface this project has, and it is the one not registered.
Nothing records that the live file corresponds to release **0.2.0**.
*Suggested fix:* register it with `documents: {tokens_version: "0.2.0"}` and the file key.

### INFO

**I-1 · The `fontFamily` array → STRING flattening is performed by the importer and declared nowhere.**
`tokens.json` holds an 8-element fallback stack; Figma holds it comma-joined with no spaces.
Verified: `",".join(source) == live` exactly for both families, and `", ".join(...)` does **not** match.
The generated file emits a JSON array; the contract says only `fontFamily → STRING`. A future importer
choosing `", "` would change both values and nothing would flag it.
*Suggested fix:* declare the separator in the contract, or have the generator emit the joined string.

**I-2 · Five tracking values differ by 1.8 × 10⁻⁹ to 2.15 × 10⁻⁸ px; 289 palette colours by up to
2.96 × 10⁻⁸ per channel.** Float32 residue, visually meaningless, recorded for two reasons: it is the
fingerprint behind W-1, and `check-figma-live.py`'s 1e-4 tolerance means a *genuine* 0.0001px-class
error in the same fields would be indistinguishable from it.

**I-3 · Mode order is inferred, not proven.** `Light` is the first key in every captured `semantic`
entry's `modes` object, consistent with Light being `collection.modes[0]` — the default an
unconfigured frame inherits. Key order in a serialised capture is not proof. If Dark were index 0,
every unconfigured consumer would render dark and nothing here would show it.

## What was verified how

### Verified by re-derivation from `tokens.json`

- 829 leaves; 32 non-representable by the contract's own type table; 797 representable. Derived without
  importing the generator, then confirmed against it: 797/797 paths, 0 type mismatches, 0 value
  mismatches. **The generator faithfully implements the contract.**
- 797/797 expected rows present in the live capture at `(collection, name, mode)`. 0 missing, 0 extra.
- 474 alias comparisons exact; 289 colour comparisons exact across 1156 channels; 32 numeric
  comparisons exact; 2 string comparisons exact. 0 uncompared.
- 35 alpha primitives, alpha and hex byte both exact; 53 semantic→alpha bindings, all correct in the
  mode the source names; 0 unexplained opaque bindings.
- Mode collapse: 236/236 Dark aliases against the source; the 13 legitimately-identical names match
  exactly, proving Dark is not a copy of Light.
- Cross-corroboration against the independent 2026-09-01 pre-collapse capture: 0 names lost, 0 gained,
  53 alias changes all of the C-021 form, 35 palette additions all alpha-suffixed, 254 surviving
  literals unchanged, three other collections untouched.
- Internal integrity of the live file: 0 duplicates, 0 dangling aliases, 5 collections.
- Read-only cross-checks run: `figma-representable.py` (797 importable, PASS),
  `build-figma-tokens.py --check` (current), `check-value-modifiers.py` (53 verified, 0 inert).

### Taken from the capture on trust

- That the capture is **complete and current** for file `ip2wZ3UUQ5sbFc3r902kYK`. Question 5's "0 extra"
  is exactly as strong as this assumption and no stronger — an omitted variable is indistinguishable
  from an absent one.
- That the mode labelled `Dark` is the mode a consumer selecting Dark receives, and that Light and Dark
  belong to one collection.
- Variable IDs, `hiddenFromPublishing`, `codeSyntax`, and library/remote state are absent from the
  capture entirely.

### NOT verified at all — skipped is not passed

1. **The 8 text styles and the 2 effect styles.** No capture exists; none reached me. Question 6 is
   unanswered as a measurement. §6 records the specification to check against, nothing more.
2. **Whether anything still references the deleted `semantic-dark` variable IDs.** The collapse was
   done by Plugin API, so the Dark values now live on the *Light* variables' IDs and the old
   `semantic-dark` IDs no longer exist. Any effect style, component binding, published-library
   consumer, or other Figma file bound to one of those 236 IDs now holds a dangling reference. **This
   is the one way the collapse could still have lost something my alias comparison cannot see**, and I
   could not look. Anything that consumed `semantic-dark` before today should be opened and checked
   by something that can drive Figma.
3. **Non-variable content.** Paint styles, grid styles, components, component sets, pages, detached
   layers. Question 5 is answered for variables only.
4. **Mode index order** (I-3).
5. **Currency.** Everything here is one capture old and I cannot drive Figma. Any edit to the live file
   since 2026-09-02 invalidates all of it; re-capture before relying on these results.

---

## Severity summary

| Sev | # | Findings |
|---|---|---|
| Blocker | 2 | B-1 drift checker non-functional · B-2 generated file no longer importable |
| Error | 1 | E-1 161 Dark descriptions lost, 24 substantive |
| Warning | 6 | W-1 provenance · W-2 zero scoping · W-3 shadow figma_home · W-4 stale elevation note · W-5 tracking pairing exception · W-6 surface unregistered |
| Info | 3 | I-1 fontFamily join undeclared · I-2 float32 residue · I-3 mode order inferred |
| Not verified | 5 | styles · dangling variable IDs · non-variable content · mode index · currency |

**Values: clean. Instrumentation: broken.** The mirror is correct today by a margin that three
independent lines of evidence agree on, and there is currently nothing that would tell anyone when it
stops being correct — least of all in Dark mode, where being wrong is unrecoverable.
